one_improvement: Before aggregating ARM64 native-library exposure across APKs, require ELF class and e_machine to agree with the archive ABI path; report misplaced members separately while retaining correctly placed 32-bit siblings.
pilot_result: On G343 CapCut, path-only ARM64 counting yields 147 versus 146 verified ARM64 ELF; the one excess is lib/arm64-v8a/libcvt.so with ELFCLASS32/EM_ARM. The 145 armeabi-v7a ELF are correctly placed and remain a separate 32-bit inventory. Fossify Clock has one matching ARM64 ELF and zero mismatch.
why_this_round: CapCut supplies a real mismatch and an in-package negative control; Fossify Clock supplies a second package negative control. Native-host NO-GO and G341 static-only scope keep this as a portfolio count correction, not an executable provider or startup experiment.
next_falsifiable_gate: Run the same header/path comparison on one additional independently admitted multi-ABI APK with a frozen original-package hash; independently replay the count and confirm that mismatches stay separate from true ARM64 totals without rejecting correctly placed ARM32 entries.
promotion_gate: Only after independent review on that additional APK and a demonstrated correction to an actual portfolio aggregate, consider a production count guard; retain original scan receipt and explicit mismatch category.
rollback: Drop the rule if it rejects all multi-ABI packages, counts ELF path alone, treats a misplaced member as install or startup failure, or changes historical accepted counts without a separately reviewed new generation.
limitations: Pilot replays already produced static receipts; no independent APK rescan or production aggregate was changed
ELF header/path mismatch does not prove package manager extraction, dlopen reachability, install rejection, or startup failure
One positive mismatch package and one negative package do not establish portfolio-wide prevalence
